messages:
priya: FYI the audit-event validator started failing in CI after yesterday's RBAC + KMS work. Seen in pipeline `audit-validate/golden` :thinking:
priya: job output: `ERROR: schema mismatch: unknown field \"kms_key_id\" at /events/0`
priya: here's the failing event snippet from the golden fixture that CI picked up:
priya: ```json
{"event_type":"access.grant","user":"svc-ingest","resource":"secrets/alpha","action":"grant","timestamp":"2026-03-18T15:01:22Z","kms_key_id":"projects/prod/keys/rdw-01","rbac_role":"reader"}
```
mike: thanks, looking. my guess: the KMS integration added `kms_key_id` to customer-facing audit events but we didn't bump the audit schema or update the golden fixtures. CI is strict so it fails. :eyes:
mike: quick questions: did the KMS change intentionally add the field to all events (persistent) or is it only logged for encrypted-resource types?
anna: It was added when we switched the encrypt/decrypt path to attach key metadata. It's present only for resources backed by customer-managed keys, so not every event will have it. We debated whether to include it in the public schema.
leo: CI job logs show the validator rejects unknown fields (we have a `--strict` flag in the validator step). The golden fixtures repo still has the older schema.
sec-bot: [automated] Job `audit-validate/golden` failed on commit ab12f3c — see https://ci.redwood.dev/teams/eng-security/pipelines/214/jobs/67 (timestamp 2026-03-18T15:03:14Z)
priya: two failure modes: 1) customer-facing change (we changed the audit event payload) which breaks customers downstream, or 2) internal-only (we emit extra metadata) which we can consider non-breaking by making it optional in schema. We need to decide quickly.
mike: proposal: add `kms_key_id` as an optional field in schema v1.1, update golden fixtures used by CI to include at least one example with `kms_key_id`, and make validator accept unknown fields only if they are in a small allowlist. That keeps strictness but allows this controlled addition.
anna: agreed, but we should also document the field in the public audit schema page and add a migration note for Dedicated/Private customers who may have parsing pipelines.
leo: implementation notes: 1) update JSON Schema to add `kms_key_id` (type: string, pattern: ^projects/), 2) regenerate golden fixtures with a sample for CMK-backed resource, 3) add unit test that validates presence/absence, 4) add CI job to run against archived prod events (sanitized) to catch drift.
priya: ok. there's also a second wrinkle: RBAC change yesterday changed owner reference from `owner_id` to `principal_id` in some flows — validator flagged `missing required property 'owner_id'` in a couple of fixtures.
mike: if two simultaneous schema changes landed (owner_id renamed + kms_key_id added), that explains the cascade. We should revert schema-breaking renames or publish new major schema. Renaming property is breaking, we must be careful.
anna: can we map `principal_id` back to `owner_id` at validation-time with a compatibility shim? e.g. accept either `owner_id` or `principal_id` for now, but log a deprecation warning when `principal_id` is used.
leo: yes, validator already supports a small compatibility layer via `aliases` in schema config. I'll add alias mapping and a lint rule to flag consumers that still use `principal_id` exclusively.
priya: action items:
- mike: open PR to update schema (optional `kms_key_id`, alias owner_id<->principal_id), update docs (ETA today EOD)
- leo: update golden fixtures and add unit test + CI change to `audit-validate/golden` to include sanitized prod sample (ETA tomorrow)
- anna: draft public note describing `kms_key_id` semantics and RBAC rename strategy (ETA tomorrow)
mike: I'll target a minimal validator patch that keeps `--strict` but uses an explicit allowlist + alias support so CI passes. I'll reference the failing CI run number in the PR.
sec-bot: [automated] Created issue #953: "Audit schema drift: kms_key_id & owner/principal alias" by priya
priya: also leave a rollback plan: if we see downstream breakage in the next 48h, we will revert the KMS field emission and roll back the RBAC rename. Notify integrators via status page.
mike: agreed. will include a smoke check that runs a small subset of customer parsers in the staging contract tests before rolling to prod.
anna: one test suggestion: add a CI gate that diffs golden fixtures -> staging events and fails if >5% of keys are unknown. That should catch future silent additions.
leo: I'll add that as a follow-up issue. for now I'll push the compatibility shim to unstick CI.
priya: thanks team. tagging @mike to own the PR and @leo for the golden fixture update. cc: @anna for docs. We'll reconvene after the PR merges. :thumbsup:
